name: Migration Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public migration data.

entries.title: CBP Nationwide and Southwest Land Border Encounters
entries.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection monthly encounter counts: U.S. Border Patrol Title 8 apprehensions, Office of Field Operations Title 8 inadmissibles, and Title 42 expulsions (March 2020 to May 2023), nationwide and for the southwest land border, by area of responsibility, state, citizenship and demographic group. The most-cited series on US border crossings.

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

coverage.spatial: United States (nationwide; by CBP area of responsibility, state, USBP sector and OFO field office)
coverage.temporal: FY2020-present in the current CSVs (FY23-FY26 rolling file); older summary pages from FY2017

entries.attribution: U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Nationwide Encounters (CBP Public Data Portal)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (headless Chromium; plain curl with a browser User-Agent got HTTP 403 from the CDN, so this site needs a headless browser). This is the CBP Public Data Portal dataset page behind the Nationwide Encounters dashboard (https://www.cbp.gov/newsroom/stats/nationwide-encounters) and the Southwest Land Border Encounters dashboard (https://www.cbp.gov/newsroom/stats/southwest-land-border-encounters, page "Last Modified: Sep 16, 2026"; its own CSVs are at https://www.cbp.gov/document/stats/southwest-land-border-encounters). The page offers CSVs "by Area of Responsibility" and "by State" plus a data dictionary PDF dated 09/29/2023. The newest file on the day checked was "Nationwide Encounters Dataset FY23-FY26 by Area of Responsibility - August", CSV dated 09/04/2026; monthly files were posted from 11/05/2025 (October) through 09/04/2026 (August). The dashboards say "Data is extracted from live CBP systems and data sources. Statistical information is subject to change ... Final statistics are available at the conclusion of each fiscal year." The data portal adds that "All analyses produced using these datasets are considered unofficial unless provided directly from CBP." No discontinuation notice was seen.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.cbp.gov/site-policy-notices/copyright-notice says "Unless a copyright is indicated, information on the U.S. Customs and Border Protection website is in the public domain and may be reproduced, published or otherwise used without the permission of the CBP. We request only that the CBP be cited as the source of the information". This is a site-wide notice, not a data-specific licence. Not checked: CSV contents or column definitions, and the by-component dashboard.

entries.title: DHS OHSS Yearbook of Immigration Statistics
entries.description: The Department of Homeland Security's annual compendium of US immigration flow tables by fiscal year: lawful permanent residents, refugees, asylees, naturalizations, nonimmigrant (temporary visitor) admissions, and immigration enforcement actions (apprehensions, removals, returns). Published by the DHS Office of Homeland Security Statistics (OHSS), formerly the Office of Immigration Statistics.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Office of Homeland Security Statistics (OHSS)

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

coverage.spatial: United States (national; some tables by state, country of birth or citizenship)
coverage.temporal: yearbooks FY1996-FY2024 listed (FY2024 tables partly released)

entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Office of Homeland Security Statistics, Yearbook of Immigration Statistics
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (headless Chromium; plain curl with a browser User-Agent got HTTP 403 from the CDN, so this site needs a headless browser). The index page lists yearbooks 1996 through 2024 and says "We release data tables as they become available. We release the final yearbook PDF in September of the following fiscal year." On the day checked, the 2024 and 2023 yearbooks both showed "Download coming soon" in place of a PDF; the newest PDF listed was the 2022 Yearbook. Index page "Last updated: August 20, 2025". The 2024 yearbook page ("Last updated: August 11, 2026") offers xlsx and HTML tables for LPRs, refugees, asylees, naturalizations and nonimmigrant admissions ("available now"), while "Tables 34-43: Enforcement Actions (coming soon)". The related OHSS "Immigration Enforcement and Legal Processes Monthly Tables" page (https://ohss.dhs.gov/topics/immigration/immigration-enforcement/monthly-tables) states "This monthly report is delayed while it is under review."; its newest file is the November 2024 table, and the page shows "Last updated: January 16, 2025". The monthly tables are not cataloged as a separate entry for that reason.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: no OHSS- or DHS-specific data licence or copyright page was found (https://www.dhs.gov/website-policies returned 404; https://www.dhs.gov/privacy-policy covers privacy only). The public-domain status rests on the work being produced by a federal agency (17 U.S.C. 105), not on a published data licence. Not checked: the table contents, the data dictionary, or whether earlier yearbooks were revised.

entries.title: EOIR Workload and Adjudication Statistics
entries.description: The Department of Justice Executive Office for Immigration Review's official statistics on the US immigration courts and Board of Immigration Appeals: pending cases, new cases and completions, decision outcomes, asylum applications and decisions, in absentia removal orders, representation rates, unaccompanied children's cases, appeals and immigration judge hiring. The government's own count of the immigration court backlog.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR)

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

coverage.spatial: United States (national; some tables by state or court)
coverage.temporal: varies by table (FY 2026 decision outcomes latest; historical new cases and completions table)

entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Justice, Executive Office for Immigration Review, Workload and Adjudication Statistics
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (plain curl with a browser User-Agent and headless Chromium both returned 200; no headless browser needed). The page lists 22 numbered PDF tables under Caseload ("Pending Cases, New Cases, and Total Completions", "FY 2026 Decision Outcomes"), Amnesty Cases, Asylum ("Asylum Decisions", "Total Asylum Applications"), In Absentia, Motions, Representation, Unaccompanied Alien Children, Remote Hearings, Board of Immigration Appeals, OCAHO and Immigration Judge Corps. It says "EOIR staff frequently enter and update information into the case database, so the statistics provided are subject to change" and "statistics for FYs 2020 and 2021 may have been affected by operational disruptions caused by COVID-19." Page footer: "Updated October 20, 2026". No release schedule, delay or discontinuation notice was seen. Duplicate check: justice-almanac has no EOIR entry. The tables are PDF summaries; EOIR's case-level data is released separately through its FOIA library, which I did not check.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.justice.gov/legalpolicies, under "Copyright Status and Citation", says "Unless otherwise indicated, information on Department of Justice websites is in the public domain and may be copied and distributed without permission. Citation of the Department of Justice as source of the information is appreciated". This is a site-wide policy, not a data-specific licence. Not checked: individual PDF contents or their data-as-of dates.

entries.title: Eurostat Migration and Asylum Statistics
entries.description: Eurostat's statistics on migration and asylum in the EU and EFTA: immigration and emigration flows and citizenship acquisitions, asylum applications and first-instance and final decisions, Dublin transfers, resettlement, temporary protection for people fleeing Ukraine, residence permits, and enforcement of immigration legislation (refusals at the border, third-country nationals found illegally present, return orders and returns).

coverage.spatial: EU member states and EFTA countries (some series include candidate countries)
coverage.temporal: varies by dataset (monthly asylum data to July 2026 latest seen)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Eurostat copyright notice and free re-use of data)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The theme page "Migration and asylum" is "an entry point to the wide range of Eurostat statistics on migration and asylum" and splits into International migration, citizenship; Asylum; Managed migration ("residence permits issued, refusals at border, persons apprehended inside of the territory or persons subject to return"); Children in migration; and Migrant integration. Latest news: "Asylum applications in July 2026" (23 October 2026), "Temporary protection for 4.43 million in August 2026" (12 October 2026) and "Returns to third countries up by 10% in Q2 2026" (30 September 2026). The cadence is monthly for asylum and temporary protection; managed-migration series are quarterly or annual. The asylum database page https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/migration-asylum/asylum/database answered HTTP 200 but wasn't read in detail. population-almanac's eurostat-population-and-demography covers population stocks and net migration as a component of change; this entry covers the flows, asylum and enforcement theme. Its immigration and emigration flow tables (migr_imm*, migr_emi*) sit in this theme. Formats and API/bulk access come from Eurostat's site-wide data tools and weren't checked per dataset.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: Eurostat copyright notice (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice, HTTP 200): "The copyright for the editorial content of this website, which is owned by the EU, is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence." and "Reuse of statistical data, metadata, publications, and other dissemination tools published on this website for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged." The licence string matches the other verticals' Eurostat entries.

entries.title: Frontex Migratory Map and Detections of Illegal Border-Crossings
entries.description: Frontex's monthly statistics on detections of illegal border-crossings at the EU's external borders, by migratory route (Central Mediterranean, Western Balkans, Eastern Mediterranean and others), border type and nationality, behind its interactive Migratory Map. The most-cited series on irregular arrivals to the EU.
entries.publisher: Frontex, European Border and Coast Guard Agency

coverage.spatial: EU and Schengen-associated external borders, by route and nationality
coverage.temporal: not checked (data as of October 2026 latest)

entries.license: proprietary (Frontex legal disclaimer; private use only, other reuse needs Frontex permission)
entries.attribution: Frontex, Detections of illegal border-crossings (FRAN and JORA data)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page "Migratory Map" says "This map presents the current migratory situation in Europe. Each circle represents one of the main migratory routes into the EU." It links "Detections of illegal border-crossings statistics download (updated monthly)" to Monthly_detections_of_IBC_2026_10_05.xlsx (HTTP 200, about 1.5 MB, not opened) with "Source: FRAN and JORA data as of October 2026." It cautions that "The data presented refer to detections of illegal border-crossing rather than the number of persons, as the same person may cross the external border several times." The map itself is an embedded viewer and wasn't inspected. The start year and breakdowns in the spreadsheet weren't checked. The download file name changes each month, so the landing page is cataloged.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: Frontex legal disclaimer (https://www.frontex.europa.eu/legal-disclaimer/, HTTP 200), Copyright Notice: "This site and its content are the copyright of Frontex with the exception of the legal instruments. ... The materials provided on this website may be used for private purposes in accordance with applicable legal provisions. For use, reproduction or transmission for purposes other than private use, please request permission from Frontex." It's site-wide; no data-specific licence was found. Restrictive: the entry links to the data but doesn't imply it can be redistributed. The attribution string is the curator's (no citation format found).

entries.title: ICE Detention Statistics (fiscal-year spreadsheets)
entries.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody data published as fiscal-year spreadsheets: detention population and book-ins, alternatives to detention, and facility-level detention counts with footnotes. The primary federal source for how many people ICE holds and where.
entries.publisher: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Enforcement and Removal Operations

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

coverage.spatial: United States (national and by detention facility)

entries.attribution: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Detention Statistics
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (headless Chromium; plain curl with a browser User-Agent got HTTP 403 from the CDN, so this site needs a headless browser). The "Detention Statistics" section of the Detention Management page says "The data tables are searchable and sortable, and worksheets are protected ... Data may fluctuate until it is locked at the conclusion of the fiscal year." It lists "FY 2026 ICE Statistics" (Detention FY 2026 YTD, Alternatives to Detention FY 2026 YTD and Facilities FY 2026 YTD, Footnotes), linked as FY26_detentionStats07202026.xlsx, and "FY 2025 ICE Statistics" linked as FY25_detentionStats09242025.xlsx, plus "Previous Year-End Reports" for FY2019 through FY2024 and an Over-72-hour facilities list. The page footer reads "Updated: 10/27/2026", but the newest spreadsheet's filename carries the date 07/20/2026. No FY2025 year-end report appears under "Previous Year-End Reports" (the list starts at FY2024). No release schedule is stated on this page. The related ERO Statistics Dashboard (https://www.ice.gov/statistics) says its dashboards show data "as of December 31, 2024. The dashboards will be updated quarterly" and its own footer reads "Updated: 07/24/2026"; that dashboard was not cataloged separately.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.ice.gov/site-policies, under "Copyright", says "Information presented on the ICE Website is considered public information and may be distributed or copied. However, ICE does request that the use of appropriate byline/photo/image credit is given to ICE." This is a site-wide policy, not a data-specific licence. Not checked: spreadsheet contents, footnotes, or whether past files were revised.

entries.title: IDMC Global Internal Displacement Database (GIDD)
entries.description: The Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre's validated annual estimates of internal displacements (new movements) and internally displaced people at year end, by country and by cause (conflict and violence, disasters), with event-level disaggregated data. The standard global reference for internal displacement figures.
entries.publisher: Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC), part of the Norwegian Refugee Council

access.auth_note: API access requires a key requested from IDMC; web downloads need none

entries.license: CC-BY-3.0-IGO (IDMC website terms of use, site-wide)
entries.attribution: Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC), Global Internal Displacement Database
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl). The page renders its figures with JavaScript, so it was read in headless Chromium. It heads "Global Internal Displacement Database (GIDD)" and "IDMC's global repository of internal displacement data, covering since 2008", shows "Validated figures for 2008-2025 globally · 214 countries and territories" (82.5m IDPs as of 2025), and offers "Disaggregated data for 2025" as GeoJSON and Excel plus "Annual displacement data" as Excel. It says "For provisional data from the past 180 days, consult the Internal Displacement Unit (IDU). To request an API key, read the documentation." The API documentation and the IDU weren't opened. UNHCR's API also redistributes IDMC figures (idmc endpoint).
Licence checked 2026-10-31: IDMC terms of use (https://www.internal-displacement.org/terms-of-use/, HTTP 200), "Using our content": "Unless specified otherwise in particular terms of use, anyone may reproduce, distribute, adapt, translate and publicly perform the content on this website, without explicit permission, provided that the content is accompanied by an acknowledgement that IDMC is the source ... This is in line with the Creative Commons – Attribution (BY) 3.0 IGO – license." It's a site-wide statement, not a data-specific licence, and the API may carry its own terms (not checked).

entries.title: IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
entries.description: IOM's system for tracking and monitoring displacement and population mobility in crises: baseline and mobility-tracking assessments of internally displaced people and returnees, flow monitoring along migration routes, registration and surveys, published as country reports, datasets, maps and an API. A primary operational source for displacement figures in Sudan, Ukraine, Yemen, the Sahel and elsewhere.

access.auth_note: The DTM API (v3) needs a free account and subscription key from the DTM Developer Portal; reports and public datasets need none

coverage.spatial: crisis-affected countries where DTM operates (country, Admin 1 and Admin 2 levels)

entries.license: proprietary (DTM Terms & Conditions; non-commercial viewing, download and print only, no redistribution or derivatives without IOM permission)
entries.attribution: International Organization for Migration (IOM), [month and year of publication]. DTM [title of publication]. IOM, [place of publication].
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 403. curl (browser user agent) and headless Chromium both got an Akamai "Access Denied" page. The site was read only through WebFetch, which did get the page content; the link checker may see 403. WebFetch showed the DTM homepage with "Data and analysis" (reports, datasets, maps, API), country pages, and recent datasets dated late October 2026, among them a Sudan displacement and return snapshot (27 October 2026) and a Yemen Rapid Displacement Tracking dataset (18-24 October 2026). The API page (https://dtm.iom.int/data-and-analysis/dtm-api, also via WebFetch) describes an IDP API (country, Admin 1, Admin 2) and an HNA API, "non-sensitive, aggregated figures" only, with registration and a subscription key required, and says version 3 went live in August 2025. API response formats weren't stated or checked, so `format` is omitted. The IOM Migration Data Portal (migrationdataportal.org), a separate IOM site, returned 403 to every client and isn't cataloged.
Licence checked 2026-10-31 (via WebFetch, so the quotes passed through a summariser): DTM Terms & Conditions (https://dtm.iom.int/terms-and-conditions): "The Materials may be viewed, downloaded, and printed for non-commercial use only, without, inter alia, any right to sell, resell, redistribute or create derivative works therefrom", and "Any extraction, translation, reproduction, and distribution ... requires the explicit prior written permission of IOM." No open licence is named. Some DTM datasets are also posted on HDX, where they may carry a different licence; that wasn't checked. These are restrictive terms: the entry links to the data but doesn't imply it can be reused.

entries.title: IOM Migration Data Portal
entries.description: IOM's portal of international migration statistics, compiled from more than 25 data providers: an interactive world map of internationally comparable indicators (immigration, emigration, labour migration, remittances, missing migrants, refugees, internal displacement and more), key global figures, a data catalogue, and thematic and regional overviews explaining the sources.
entries.publisher: International Organization for Migration (IOM), Global Data Institute

coverage.spatial: Global (country level; national data for four pilot countries)
coverage.temporal: varies by indicator and source (not checked)

entries.license: unverified — the portal's Terms of use page (https://www.migrationdataportal.org/terms-use) answered HTTP 503 "Site under maintenance" to every client on 2026-11-01; most data are secondary, from UN DESA, UNICEF and other providers
entries.attribution: International Organization for Migration (IOM), Migration Data Portal (cite the original data provider shown for each indicator)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (plain curl, and headless Chromium in new headless mode). curl with a browser User-Agent got HTTP 403, so the block seen on 2026-10-31 appears to depend on the client. The About page says the site "is designed to help policy makers, national statistics officers, journalists and the general public interested in the field of migration to navigate the increasingly complex landscape of international migration data". It says the interactive world map "visualizes international, publicly-available and internationally comparable migration data", that national data cover "four pilot countries -- Switzerland, South Africa, New Zealand and Germany", that "An inventory of all public data available in the Portal's database and interactive dashboards can be found in the data catalogue" (https://www.migrationdataportal.org/data-catalogue), and that "The Portal features secondary data from more than 25 data providers and data sources". The home page says "All data is from international sources, such as UN DESA and UNICEF." It complements iom-displacement-tracking-matrix. Download formats, an API and update cadence were not checked, so format is left empty.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: not verified. The footer links "Terms of use" at https://www.migrationdataportal.org/terms-use, which answered HTTP 503 with "The Migration Data Portal is currently under maintenance and will be back online shortly" to curl and headless Chromium on several attempts, while other pages loaded; WebFetch got 403. No licence is asserted. Because the data are secondary, the original providers' terms also apply. IOM's DTM terms are restrictive (see iom-displacement-tracking-matrix), but I did not assume they cover this portal.

entries.title: IRCC Open Data – Monthly IRCC Updates
entries.description: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's open datasets on the Canadian immigration system, led by the "Monthly IRCC Updates" series: new permanent residents by category, province and country of citizenship, asylum claimants, study and work permit holders, temporary-to-permanent transitions, Express Entry invitations, and operational processing. The official source for Canadian admissions and asylum claim counts.

coverage.spatial: Canada (national, province/territory; by country of citizenship)
coverage.temporal: varies by dataset (2015 onward for most monthly series; not checked per dataset)

entries.license: OGL-Canada-2.0 (Open Government Licence – Canada, per each dataset record)
entries.attribution: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, Monthly IRCC Updates (Open Government Portal)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The IRCC organisation URL https://open.canada.ca/data/en/organization/cic redirects to this search page, which says "Found 62 records" with "Asylum Claimants – Monthly IRCC Updates" first ("Record Modified: Oct 22, 2026 ... Formats: HTML XLSX CSV"). The CKAN API (https://open.canada.ca/data/api/action/package_search, HTTP 200, no key) lists 12 "Monthly IRCC Updates" datasets, including Permanent Residents (id f7e5498e-0ad8-4417-85c9-9b8aff9b9eda, monthly, 52 CSV/XLSX resources, modified 2026-10-20), Asylum Claimants (b6cbcf4d-f763-4924-a2fb-8cc4a06e3de4), study permit and TFWP/IMP work permit holders, and archived Syrian, Afghan and Resettled Refugees series. The Permanent Residents description warns: "Values between 0 and 5 are shown as “--“ and all other values are rounded to the nearest multiple of 5." The 2015 start year is from general knowledge and wasn't checked. Statistics Canada's immigration subject page (https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/subjects/immigration_and_ethnocultural_diversity) redirected to the generic subjects index and isn't cataloged; its content is mostly about the stock of immigrants (census), which belongs to population-almanac.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: every Monthly IRCC Updates record returned by the API has license_title "Open Government Licence - Canada" (https://open.canada.ca/en/open-government-licence-canada). That licence page says "The Information Provider grants you a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use the Information, including for commercial purposes" and that you must "Acknowledge the source of the Information by including any attribution statement specified by the Information Provider(s)". The licence page text includes "version 2.0".

entries.title: Mexico UPMRIP Migration Statistics Bulletins (Boletines estadísticos)
entries.description: Mexico's official migration statistics from the Unidad de Política Migratoria, Registro e Identidad de Personas (Secretaría de Gobernación): monthly and annual statistical bulletins and data tables on entries, documentation and stay status of foreigners, people in an irregular migration situation presented to the immigration authority, protection of migrants, and returns of Mexicans from the United States and Canada. The key official source on migration through and from Mexico.
entries.publisher: Unidad de Política Migratoria, Registro e Identidad de Personas (UPMRIP), Secretaría de Gobernación

coverage.spatial: Mexico (national; by state and nationality in some tables)

entries.license: unverified — no data licence on the page; the gob.mx portal terms (gob.mx/terminos) allow viewing and download for personal, non-commercial use only
entries.attribution: Unidad de Política Migratoria, Registro e Identidad de Personas, SEGOB, Boletín estadístico
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200, but the response is a 730-byte "Error ... This page can't be displayed. Contact support" page (a web application firewall) for curl with a browser user agent and for headless Chromium alike. The content was read only through WebFetch, so the link checker will probably see this error page. WebFetch shows the Dirección de Estadística page of the UPMRIP with "Boletines estadísticos" (a 2026 monthly bulletin and annual bulletins 2002-2025) and "Cuadros de datos (2026)" on entries, documentation and stay status, people in an irregular migration situation, protection groups, and returns of Mexicans from the United States and Canada. The month of the latest bulletin wasn't shown. File formats weren't checked, so `format` is omitted. The former host politicamigratoria.gob.mx didn't answer (connection failed).
Licence checked 2026-10-31, NOT verified for the data: the bulletins page has no licence statement. The gob.mx portal terms (https://www.gob.mx/terminos, HTTP 200) say "Se autoriza al Usuario a visualizar y descargar los materiales contenidos en el sitio solamente para su uso personal y no para un uso comercial" and "El Usuario no deberá modificar, reproducir o mostrar pública o comercialmente los materiales". It's not certain those portal-wide terms govern these statistics (the page sits on portales.segob.gob.mx). Mexico's open data licence (Libre Uso MX) applies only to datasets on datos.gob.mx, which returned an Akamai 403 and couldn't be searched for an equivalent dataset.

entries.title: Migración Colombia – Entradas de extranjeros a Colombia
entries.description: Migración Colombia's monthly counts of foreign nationals entering Colombia since 2012, by nationality, sex and migration control post, published on Colombia's open data portal. One of a family of Migración Colombia datasets there (departures of Colombians, Venezuelan entries, temporary protection pre-registrations) covering the main Latin American migration corridor.

coverage.spatial: Colombia (national, by migration control post), by nationality

entries.attribution: Unidad Administrativa Especial Migración Colombia, Entradas de extranjeros a Colombia (datos.gov.co)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The short URL https://www.datos.gov.co/d/96sh-4v8d redirects to the canonical URL. The dataset metadata (https://www.datos.gov.co/api/views/96sh-4v8d.json) reads "Muestra el consolidado de entradas de extranjeros a Colombia desde el 2012, discriminado por nacionalidad y género", with columns Año, Mes, Nacionalidad, Codigo M49, Femenino, Masculino, Indefinido, Total and Ubicación PCM. The rows were last updated 20 August 2026. The SODA API (/resource/96sh-4v8d.json, no key) returned 181,186 rows with a maximum year of 2026. The stated update frequency is "Semestral", so cadence is irregular (the schema has no semiannual value). Related Migración Colombia datasets on the portal: Salidas de colombianos desde el territorio nacional (efw5-jiej), MIGRANTES A COLOMBIA (c4mm-qn8q), and Pre registros Estatuto Temporal de Protección para Migrantes Venezolanos (6eyy-q57b). Migración Colombia's own site (https://www.migracioncolombia.gov.co/, HTTP 200) has a "Planeación y Estadística" section that wasn't explored. CSV/JSON formats come from the standard Socrata exports; only JSON was fetched.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the dataset's own metadata gives license "Creative Commons Attribution | Share Alike 4.0 International" (licenseId CC_40_BY_SA, termsLink http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode). It's a dataset-specific licence. The other Migración Colombia datasets listed above carry the same licence in the portal catalog.

entries.title: OECD International Migration Database
entries.description: OECD's annual series, provided mostly by national correspondents of the OECD Expert Group on Migration, on inflows and outflows of foreign population and inflows of asylum seekers by nationality, stocks of foreign population, and acquisitions of nationality, for OECD countries. Companion dataflows give standardised permanent and temporary inflows. The basis of the annual International Migration Outlook.
entries.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)

coverage.spatial: OECD member countries (destination), by country of nationality
coverage.temporal: varies by country and series (2024 latest year seen)

entries.license: unverified — OECD terms page (oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html) is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge and could not be read
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. OECD Data Explorer is a JavaScript app; it was read in headless Chromium, titled "OECD Data Explorer • International migration database", with a default view of "Inflows of foreign population" from 2012. The dataset page on oecd.org (https://www.oecd.org/en/data/datasets/international-migration-database.html) returned a Cloudflare 403. The SDMX dataflow OECD.ELS.IMD:DSD_MIG@DF_MIG (https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/, HTTP 200, no key) describes it: "annual series on flows of foreign population and of asylum seekers by nationality, stocks of foreign population by nationality, as well as acquisitions of nationality by former nationality ... based on national concepts and definitions and therefore are not fully comparable across countries." Among the latest observations in a CSV pull, the most common years were 2023 and 2024. The same agency publishes related dataflows: DF_MIG_POPF (foreign-born stocks), DF_MIG_INT_PER and DF_MIG_INT_TEMP (standardised permanent and temporary inflows), and labour-market outcomes of immigrants. Foreign-population stocks overlap with population-almanac's un-desa-international-migrant-stock in subject but not in source.
Licence checked 2026-10-31, NOT verified: https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html returned a Cloudflare 403 to curl, headless Chromium (two attempts) and WebFetch. labor-almanac's oecd-employment-labour-market entry quotes those terms, as read earlier, as allowing data reuse "for any purpose, even for commercial use" with the OECD citation (open with attribution, not CC BY 4.0), but this curator could not re-read them.

entries.title: US Refugee Admissions and Arrivals (Refugee Processing Center)
entries.description: The State Department Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration's monthly reports on refugees admitted through the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program (USRAP), by country of chargeability, nationality, US state of resettlement and month, plus Amerasian and Iraqi/Afghan Special Immigrant Visa arrivals. The archive holds arrivals by region since 1975 and the annual proposed-admissions reports to Congress. Formerly published as WRAPSNET.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration (Refugee Processing Center)

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

coverage.spatial: United States (national and by state of resettlement; by nationality of refugee)
coverage.temporal: 1975-present (regional totals); current fiscal year in detail (as of September 30, 2026)

entries.license: unverified — State Department public-domain notice conflicts with the RPC site's "All rights reserved" terms
entries.attribution: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration, Refugee Processing Center, Admissions & Arrivals
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (plain curl with a browser User-Agent and headless Chromium both returned 200; no headless browser needed). The old URL https://www.wrapsnet.org/admissions-and-arrivals/ returns HTTP 308 and redirects here. The page says "Reports are posted on the 5th of the following month, or the following Monday if the 5th is on a weekend" and "Historical monthly arrivals are subject to change due to reconciliation." On the day checked it offered "Refugee Admissions Report as of September 30, 2026" (xlsx) and PDFs for refugee arrivals by state and nationality, Amerasian arrivals and SIV arrivals, all as of September 30, 2026. The Archives page (https://www.rpc.state.gov/archives/) lists "Refugee Admissions by Region since 1975 as of September 30, 2026" and FY arrivals-by-region files through FY 2026. Its "Reports to Congress" list ends at "FY 2024 Report to Congress"; no FY 2025 or FY 2026 report is listed. No suspension or discontinuation notice was seen on either page. State Department visa statistics (travel.state.gov) were not cataloged in this entry.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.state.gov/copyright-information says "Unless a copyright is indicated, information on State Department websites is in the public domain and may be copied and distributed without permission. Citation of the U.S. State Department as source of the information is appreciated." However, the RPC site's own https://www.rpc.state.gov/terms-of-use/ reads, under "Copyright And Trademark Notices", "All contents of the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program Web Site are: and/or its suppliers. All rights reserved." That text looks like an unfilled template, but it is what the site says, so the licence is left unverified. Not checked: file contents and how far back the monthly archive goes.

entries.title: UK Home Office Immigration System Statistics
entries.description: The Home Office's quarterly official statistics on the UK immigration system: entry clearance visas, passenger arrivals, extensions and settlement, citizenship, asylum claims, decisions, appeals and support, resettlement, irregular migration including small boat arrivals, immigration detention and returns, and the EU Settlement Scheme.

coverage.spatial: United Kingdom (some tables by local authority)
coverage.temporal: varies by table (year ending June 2026 latest)

entries.license: OGL-UK-3.0 (Open Government Licence v3.0, GOV.UK site footer, except where otherwise stated)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The collection "Immigration system statistics quarterly release" holds 61 documents, 49 data-table pages and 3 guidance pages; the latest release is "Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026" (updated 27 August 2026, per the GOV.UK content API). The data tables page (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistical-data-sets/immigration-system-statistics-data-tables) lists asylum summary and detailed datasets, entry clearance visas, passenger arrivals, extensions, citizenship, returns, immigration detention and "Irregular migration to the UK" tables, among them "IER_D02: Number of asylum claims from small boat arrivals". It notes that "Passengers refused entry at the border" tables have been discontinued. The files seen are .xlsx and ODS; their contents weren't opened, and start years weren't checked. Some tables lag the headline release (e.g. appeals tables at year ending March 2023).
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the GOV.UK footer on the collection and data tables pages reads "All content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated". It's a site-wide statement; no data-specific licence was found on the pages.

entries.title: UNHCR Refugee Population Statistics Database (Refugee Data Finder and API)
entries.description: UNHCR's global statistics on forcibly displaced and stateless people: refugees, asylum-seekers, internally displaced persons, returnees and stateless persons by country of origin and asylum, plus asylum applications and decisions, demographics and solutions (resettlement, returns, naturalisation). The reference series for refugee figures worldwide.
entries.publisher: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
entries.license: unverified — UNHCR's dataset terms page (unhcr.org/terms-use-datasets) sits behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be read; secondary sources say CC-BY-4.0
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The canonical URL is the Refugee Statistics API documentation, which says "UNHCR's Refugee Population Statistics Database contains information about forcibly displaced populations spanning across almost 70 years of statistical activities. It covers displaced populations such as refugees, asylum-seekers and internally displaced persons, including their demographics." It lists endpoints for population, asylumApplications, asylumDecisions, demographics, solutions, idmc, unrwa and nowcasting. The API needed no key: https://api.unhcr.org/population/v1/years/ lists years from 1951, and /population/?year=2025 returned a 2025 global row (refugees 28,461,306; IDPs 64,239,352). The docs say download=true returns CSV. The public front end, the Refugee Data Finder at https://www.unhcr.org/refugee-statistics/, returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare "Just a moment..." challenge to both curl and headless Chromium (waited 20 s), so the API docs are cataloged instead; whoever can open the Data Finder may prefer it as canonical. The cadence is set to irregular because the schema has no semiannual value; UNHCR's mid-year and end-year releases are from general knowledge and weren't checked on the site. The IDMC figures inside the API duplicate the separate idmc entry.
Licence checked 2026-10-31, NOT verified: https://www.unhcr.org/terms-use-datasets returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to curl, headless Chromium and WebFetch, and no archive copy could be retrieved. A web search snippet of that page reads "Except where otherwise provided, the datasets made available by UNHCR on the UNHCR Refugee Population Statistics Database are licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution International License 4.0", and says some indicators come from third parties and "may not be shared, redistributed or reused without the consent of the original data provider". UNHCR's HDX datasets are tagged CC BY or CC BY-IGO. Treat CC-BY-4.0 as likely but confirm on the terms page before relying on it. The attribution is the database name that the snippet asks reusers to credit.

entries.title: USCIS Immigration and Citizenship Data
entries.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services' data library of quarterly and fiscal-year reports on benefit applications: receipts, approvals, denials, pending cases and processing for naturalization (N-400), green cards (I-485), family and employment petitions, employment authorization (I-765), DACA, TPS, T and U visas, special immigrant juveniles and more. The authoritative source on the legal-immigration caseload and backlog.

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

coverage.spatial: United States (national; some tables by USCIS field office, state or country)
coverage.temporal: varies by report (Fiscal Year 2026, Quarter 3 latest)

entries.attribution: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, Immigration and Citizenship Data
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (headless Chromium; plain curl with a browser User-Agent got HTTP 403 from the CDN, so this site needs a headless browser). The page leads with "Fiscal Year 2026: Quarter 3 Data Reports, April–June 2026", a curated list of XLSX files dated September 08, 2026, including "All USCIS Application and Petition Form Types", "Net Backlog and Frontlog", N-400 by field office, I-485, I-130, I-765 (including the (c)(8) pending-asylum category), DACA, TPS (I-821) by country of designation, and T/U/VAWA/SIJ reports. The searchable data library below it showed "1784 total rows". It also links the H-1B, H-2A and H-2B employer data hubs. No release schedule, delay or discontinuation notice was seen on the page. Not checked: whether an affirmative-asylum (I-589) quarterly table is in the current quarter's list (I did not see one in the curated list, but did not search the full library), file contents, or the employer data hubs.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.uscis.gov/website-policies says "Information presented on this WWW site is considered public information and may be distributed or copied. Use of appropriate byline/photo/image credit is requested." It adds that some licensed images "are not in the public domain". This is a site-wide policy, not a data-specific licence.

entries.title: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide (RPW)
entries.description: The World Bank's quarterly database of what it costs to send and receive small amounts of money between countries: fees and exchange-rate margins by service provider across 377 corridors, from 48 sending to 111 receiving countries. The source for SDG indicator 10.c.1 on remittance costs.

coverage.spatial: global (377 corridors; 48 sending and 111 receiving countries)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (World Bank Data Catalog dataset licence)
entries.attribution: The World Bank, Remittance Prices Worldwide, available at http://remittanceprices.worldbank.org
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl). The page is a JavaScript app, read in headless Chromium. The Data Catalog page "Remittance Prices Worldwide" (version 7, latest, "Metadata last updated on Sep 28, 2026") "Provides data on the cost of sending and receiving relatively small amounts of money from one country to another. Data cover 377 country corridors worldwide, from 48 remittance sending countries to 111 receiving countries." It offers DataBank views by sending country, corridor and receiving country, a "Complete Dataset" in Excel (last updated Sep 23, 2026, 48.4 MB, with an API Service link) and a quarterly report PDF (Apr 17, 2026). Temporal coverage is 2011-2025, periodicity quarter. The RPW site itself (https://remittanceprices.worldbank.org/) returned a Cloudflare 403 to curl and headless Chromium. The attribution string comes from a search-result snippet of that site and wasn't read directly. Remittance flow volumes (personal remittances received and paid) are WDI indicators, already covered by economy-almanac's world-bank-world-development-indicators, and aren't duplicated here. The old KNOMAD remittances data URL (https://www.knomad.org/data/remittances) now redirects to a World Bank brief, which says KNOMAD was "Active from 2013 until 2024".
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the Data Catalog page's "Data Access and Licensing" section reads "License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. This dataset is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0". It's a dataset-specific statement. The underlying price data are collected through a provider (FXC Intelligence, per the search snippet; not checked).
